forensic_science_laboratory_report.laboratory: Forensic Science Laboratory, Rohini, New Delhi

exhibits_received.description: Blood sample from crime scene (EDTA vial)
Victim's blood sample (from postmortem) for DNA

serology.method: Presumptive and confirmatory tests for blood, human origin, blood grouping
findings: Blood on crime scene bedsheet: Human blood, Group A+ - matches victim
Blood on victim's clothing: Human blood, Group A+
Blood on knife blade: Human blood, Group A+ - matches victim
Blood on accused's sweater: Human blood, Group A+ - MATCHES VICTIM, not accused (accused is O+)
Blood on accused's jeans: Faint blood stains, Human blood, Group A+ - matches victim
serology.conclusion: Victim's blood (A+) was found on the accused's clothing and on the recovered murder weapon. This conclusively establishes accused's physical involvement in the attack.

dna_profiling.method: STR analysis using 15 autosomal markers + Y-STR
findings: DNA from bloodstained knife handle: Mixed profile - major component matches accused Sanjay Sharma
DNA from blood on accused's sweater: Victim's DNA profile (complete match with 15/15 loci)
DNA from victim's nails: Foreign DNA recovered under right-hand fingernails - MATCHES ACCUSED at 14/15 loci
DNA from window sill (entry point): Skin cell DNA matches accused
dna_profiling.conclusion: Multiple independent DNA matches establish that: (1) Accused held the knife (handle DNA), (2) Victim's blood is on accused's clothing, (3) Accused's skin cells were under victim's fingernails indicating physical contact/struggle, (4) Accused entered through the window.

fingerprint_analysis.method: IAFIS database comparison and manual Henry classification
findings: Fingerprint on window sill: MATCHES accused's left index finger (13-point match)
Fingerprint on dining table edge: MATCHES accused's right thumb (11-point match)
Fingerprint on TV remote: MATCHES accused's left thumb (10-point match)
Partial print on knife handle area: Insufficient for identification but DNA analysis confirms
All matching prints do not correspond to victim or any other person
fingerprint_analysis.conclusion: Three clear fingerprints from the crime scene match the accused's prints, establishing his physical presence at the scene.

findings: Footwear impression from window entry: Size 10, chevron pattern, matches accused's seized shoes
Sole pattern 22-point match, wear pattern consistent

ballistics_and_weapon_analysis.method: Examination of recovered knife for class and individual characteristics
findings: Kitchen knife (8 inch blade, wooden handle)
Blood on entire blade length
Handle has victim's blood and accused's DNA
Wound pattern of victim's injuries matches this type of blade - depth, width, and edge profile consistent
ballistics_and_weapon_analysis.conclusion: The recovered kitchen knife is the murder weapon used to inflict injuries on the deceased.

findings: Accused's phone: Deleted WhatsApp messages recovered showing argument with victim about property
Victim's phone: Last call from daughter at 23:35 (unanswered)
Both phones GPS location: Accused's phone was in the vicinity of crime scene between 21:00-22:15 on 05-12-2024
Accused's phone was at his residence after 22:30

final_opinion.summary: The forensic evidence conclusively establishes the following chain: (1) The accused was present at the crime scene on the night of the murder (fingerprints, DNA, footwear impressions, GPS data); (2) The victim's blood was found on the accused's clothing and the recovered kitchen knife; (3) The accused held the murder weapon (DNA on handle); (4) The accused physically struggled with the victim (victim's nail DNA evidence); (5) The kitchen knife recovered is the actual murder weapon.
conclusive_evidence_points: Accused's DNA on murder weapon handle
Accused's DNA under victim's fingernails (physical struggle)
